title: Execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa
summary: On 10 November 1995 Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight co-defendants were hanged at Port Harcourt, Nigeria, weeks after a military tribunal convicted him of murder in October 1995. The nine were activists of the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People, and the executions were carried out by the military government.

as_recorded.value: On November 10, 1995 Saro-Wiwa and his eight co-defendants were hanged.

where.historical_name: Port Harcourt, Nigeria, under military rule

importance.justification: The executions drew international attention to the Ogoni campaign and to Nigeria's military government.

audience_note: Describes an execution by hanging of nine activists after a trial; the sources report distressing details and this record gives none.

sources.title: Nigeria kills her sun: Death and vindication for Ken Saro-Wiwa, Ogoni Nine
sources.author: Shola Lawal

reviewer_note: Port Harcourt is named by Al Jazeera ("prison grounds in Port Harcourt") and Executed Today; the Goldman page names no place. Whether the trial was fair is contested in the sources; this record states only the conviction and execution.
